shared_elements: low-relief schematic figures carved in shallow raised relief on a flat stone face
abstract non-figural signs combined with creature forms
justification: Both surfaces present shallow, flat-topped raised relief in which schematic profile creatures, arc/serpentine forms and zigzag rows are combined with abstract signs and organised into horizontal registers divided by a plain band, a fairly distinctive and conventionalised manner of laying out a broad pillar face. The clearest difference is that A is an anthropomorphic pillar whose relief functions as body imagery, with paired curving arms converging on a central disc above a belt-like band, whereas B shows purely a stacked sequence of repeated animal and zigzag rows with no anthropomorphic scheme or disc.
